Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this policy change is explicitly driven by multi-wake rollout evidence. I’ll inspect its required visual sequence, then read the workspace contract and inherited evidence before touching `solver/`.

The contract confirms one editable policy file, no CFD run, and a required pre-edit visual diagnosis. I’ve found four sampled solver rollouts; next I’m ranking them by behavior—not score alone—and tracing which inherited notes produced each mechanism.

The visuals show a consistent mechanism: all finite candidates self-propel upstream into the developed wake, then make the same late upward hook and exit; there is no collision or instability. The stronger phase allocation improves closest approach, but it also sharpens the terminal turn and raises loads, so I’m now isolating the last tested close-range variants and their parameter boundaries.

The new evidence closes the “more close-range phase boost” branch: moving from the sampled global `0.50` boost to a gated `0.55` adds upstream travel but worsens closest approach (`2.13L → 2.21L`), increases RMS loads (`535/5416 → 566/5660`), and leaves the same upper exit. I’m recording that negative boundary before implementing a single structural alternative: keep the proven far-field command, then condition close steering on body-frame lateral offset instead of the increasingly ill-conditioned angular bearing.

The candidate, provenance notes, and durable guidance lesson are all updated. I’m invoking the workspace’s mandated lightweight check-runner now; it checks the guidance delta, policy/schema contract, and editable-file boundary without running CFD.
